evidence.source: State Language Commission, General List of Simplified Chinese Characters (1986 reissue), transcription at Wikisource
evidence.field: 说明; 第一表; entry 认〔認〕
evidence.text: The list’s notes say the original traditional character is given in brackets after a simplified form; the table pairs 认〔認〕. It separately treats 讠 as a simplified component. This supports the standardized whole-character relation 認 → 认 and 言 → 讠, but does not assert an internal historical replacement 忍 → 人.
evidence.title: 简化字总表（1986年版）

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 認 is not recorded in Shuowen; describes its written left half as 言 and right half as 忍; and lists senses including identify/distinguish, agree/accept, regard as, and form a non-blood kinship. It cites Liu Kezhuang’s Song poem 《鐵塔寺》 with 細認苔間字 (“carefully identify the characters among the moss”). The cited Song example dates an identifying use, not the earliest attestation or the chronology of the other senses.
evidence.title: [A03835] 認 - 教育部《異體字字典》

Its linked original is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/19/%E5%BF%8D-seal.svg; the browser could not fetch the SVG itself. This is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph or an attested form of 認.

Direct requests for the four specified records returned internal browser errors, so no official per-character readings were inspected. Supplied local rows remain local-data claims and are not presented here as external verification.

search_audit.query: site:zh.wikisource.org 简化字总表 认〔認〕 讠; site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw 認 說文 細認苔間字 忍; Unicode Unihan U+8BA4 认 kMandarin; U+5FCD 忍; U+4EBA 人; U+8BA0 讠
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the simplified-character list, MOE dictionary entry, and exact Commons file pages. Official Unihan per-character pages returned internal errors. Exact image links were established from the Commons pages, but SVG fetches failed.

search_audit.query: Original file links from exact Commons description pages for 忍-seal.svg and 言-seal.svg; MOE dictionary historical image links
search_audit.outcome: Clicked the original SVG links and two MOE historical dictionary image links. The browser reported unsupported content type or cache misses; the source descriptions and page content remain inspected.

gaps: No dated early inscriptional form of 認 or primary paleographic account establishing its formation was found in this verification. The MOE dictionary says 認 is absent from Shuowen and describes the traditional written structure as 言 + 忍.

The Song poem is the earliest dated identifying use documented in the inspected evidence, not necessarily the earliest attestation. Dates and semantic links for accept, regard-as, kinship, and know/understand remain unresolved.

Official Unihan per-character records for 認, 认, 忍, and 人 could not be inspected. Do not present supplied local Mandarin rows as externally verified or use modern readings as proof of historical sound roles.
The exact Commons description pages establish identity, source leads, and reuse terms for modern component redrawings. Their image fetches failed in the browser, and neither image depicts 認 itself.

items.caption: Modern vector rendering of 忍 in a Shuowen seal-script style. It illustrates the analyzed sound component in traditional 認, but is not a form of 認.
items.alt: A modern vector rendering of 忍 in a seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: It illustrates 忍, which the traditional compound analysis identifies as the sound component, while keeping the image’s scope distinct from the graph 認.

items.caption: Modern vector rendering of 言 in a Shuowen seal-script style. It illustrates the speech-related component analyzed in traditional 認, but is not a form of 認.

items.selection_reason: It illustrates the speech-related 言 component in the traditional structure of 認 without suggesting the image is an early form of the whole character.

limitations.text: These modern component redrawings illustrate 言 and 忍 rather than 認. The inspected MOE dictionary states 認 is absent from Shuowen; no dated early glyph of 認 is established here.
